TURIN, Nov 15 : World number one Alexander Zverev eased past debutant Rafael Jodar in straight sets on Sunday to score an opening group win at the start of the ATP Finals in Turin. The German, a two-time champion at the season-ending tournament of the top eight players, bagged a break in each set to clinch a 6-4 6-4 victory over the 20-year-old Spaniard, who has played a sensational first season on tour and has risen from the mid-100s to the top 10 in less than 12 months. Jodar, however, could do little to tame Zverev's booming serve and the most experienced ATP Finals player in the field, playing his 31st match, earned a break to go 4-3 up with a superb backhand down the line. The Spaniard had two rare break chances at 5-4 behind but could not convert either. Instead Zverev bagged the set in the next game and grabbed a break early in the second set to open up a 3-1 lead.

Nov 15 : Rory McIlroy secured a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title on Sunday, matching Colin Montgomerie's mark for the most Order of Merit victories in European Tour history before dedicating the achievement to his recovering father. The 37-year-old Northern Irishman carded a bogey-free 67 to seal a fifth consecutive Race to Dubai crown, edging Spain's Eugenio Chacarra in the season-long standings. Englishman Tyrrell Hatton, meanwhile, cruised to a five-shot victory at the DP World Tour Championship. The latest crown capped another fine year for McIlroy, who successfully defended his Masters title at Augusta National in April to secure a second green jacket and further cement his place among the game's greats.

"I don't really know what to say. Winning eight Order of Merits was never really in my list of goals when I was growing up," McIlroy told Sky Sports. "I remember Monty (Montgomerie) being a stalwart of the European Tour. Going to watch him at the World Match Play at Wentworth over the years, I remember playing with him for the first time at the London Club on the European Tour in 2008. "To pull up alongside him and win eight of these things, it means the world to me. "I'm a proud European. I'm a proud European player and I'm proud to be a part of the DP World Tour and I'm very proud of myself right now." The milestone carried added emotional significance for McIlroy, whose father has spent the past two months recovering from major surgery. "He's been in the hospital for the last two months. He underwent a huge operation at the end of September, and he's recovering well, thankfully," McIlroy said. "But when I left to come here to the Middle East, I went up to Cleveland to see him before I went. He said to me: 'Go win the Race to Dubai.'"

Source: Reuters

BARCELONA, Nov 15 : Spanish second division team Tenerife returned to action on Sunday for the first time since the death of striker Jesus De Miguel, with emotional tributes before and during their game against Ceuta. De Miguel died on November 3, a day after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a league match at home. Tributes took place around the country and on Sunday at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium, Tenerife paid their own respects. A lengthy standing ovation bookended a minute of silence before the match. In the ninth minute play was stopped and a further round of applause followed, while a video of De Miguel was shown around the stadium, as occurred in all first and second tier games in Spain last weekend.

Tenerife forward Nacho Gil opened the scoring in the 40th minute and he celebrated by holding up De Miguel's shirt to the crowd. Gil then revealed a message written under his shirt saying "Demi (De Miguel's nickname), always in our hearts." Neal Viereck added a second four minutes from time to seal a 2-0 win for Tenerife, ending a run of six games without a win. Tenerife are 14th in the Segunda standings, while Ceuta are bottom.  Last Saturday Tenerife's game with Granada was postponed and the club invited fans to the stadium to pay their respects to De Miguel. The squad and staff were present at the Heliodoro and in Navahermosa three days earlier, where De Miguel was laid to rest.

BUCHAREST: Drones have struck three commercial ships in the Black Sea near Romania's Sulina canal, Prime Minister Luca Niculescu said on Sunday (Nov 15), adding that his armed forces had scrambled fighter jets twice. Defence Minister Stefan Radu Oprea said there were no casualties and that the ships' crews had managed to control the fires on board after the strikes late on Saturday. A growing series of deadly strikes on merchant ships near NATO members Romania and Bulgaria shows how the escalating maritime war between Russia and Ukraine is expanding into a major challenge for the transatlantic alliance in the Black Sea. The Sulina canal is a key Romanian shipping lane which links the Danube river to the Black Sea and is used by Ukraine for exports.

Romanian officials did not identify the origin of the drones but said they were a direct consequence of Russia's war in Ukraine. "These incidents are unacceptable and constitute a violation of international law," Niculescu said. "They reflect the deteriorating security situation caused by Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine." Russia has denied targeting Ukraine's neighbours with drones. Oprea said the three struck ships were Greek-flagged oil and chemical tanker Evia Petrol V, bulk carrier Marsol and oil products tanker Ali Najafov, both under the flag of Saint Kitts and Nevis. Evia Petrol V and Marsol were struck 4 and 5 nautical miles southeast of the Sulina canal, the defence ministry said, inside Romanian territorial waters. Oprea said a separate general cargo ship was hit by a drone late on Friday, also with no casualties. Private television station Digi24 said the vessel was Palau-flagged general cargo ship Larissa 1. "On Tuesday and Wednesday I will be in Brussels for the meeting with my fellow (defence) ministers," Oprea said. "We need the solidarity of our allies, shown through patrols with surveillance aircraft and through equipment for counter-drone warfare." France temporarily relocated the Atlantique 2 maritime patrols aircraft to Romania after it asked for reinforcement. Many of the ships hit in October and November were anchored near or sailing to or from the Sulina canal.

LEVI, Finland, Nov 15 : Brazil's Lucas Pinheiro Braathen won the men's World Cup slalom in Levi, Finland, on Sunday for his second victory in as many races this season. France's Clement Noel finished runner-up to Pinheiro Braathen, 0.56 seconds behind. Switzerland's Loic Meillard was third, 0.73 seconds off the pace. Starting seventh on the Levi Black course, Pinheiro Braathen led Noel by 0.65 seconds after the first run. The Brazilian skied a clean second run, giving up just nine hundredths of a second to the Frenchman. The former Norwegian racer, in his third winter competing for Brazil, has 10 World Cup victories, five of them in slalom, copying his win from last season in Levi.

Pinheiro Braathen, the Olympic giant slalom champion, also beat Meillard in last month's season opener in Soelden, Austria. "It’s rather emotional looking back one year ago in this very place where we won the first Brazilian World Cup victory in ski racing," Pinheiro Braathen said. "I'm just trying to make myself my biggest competitor and focus on the tasks at hand, the things that I’m working on in training," he added. "It is when I'm able to feel that I am having a lot of fun when I'm skiing, that I know that I'm letting go. And that's what it felt like today. Just a lot of fun." Noel will have another chance to beat Pinheiro Braathen in next Sunday's World Cup slalom in Gurgl, Austria. "The hill is different and we all know that there's going to be a lot of contenders," Noel said. "I will just try to focus on myself, ski fast and bring the confidence from Levi to Gurgl." Germany's Emma Aicher claimed the first women's World Cup slalom of the season on Saturday at the same venue.

Nov 15 : Cristiano Ronaldo Jr was watched by a number of senior internationals as he made his Portugal Under-17 debut on Thursday, playing the final 20 minutes of a 4-0 European Championship qualifying win over Andorra. Vitinha, Ruben Neves, Goncalo Ramos and Joao Felix were among those in attendance at the Portuguese FA's Cidade do Futebol complex in Oeiras, on the outskirts of Lisbon, before their own training session. For the 16-year-old Al Nassr forward, known as Cristianinho, it was another step up the international ladder — and a debut that came at a moment of changing generations. Coach Filipe Ramos named him in his 23-player squad on November 2, three days before his father retired from international football.

The eldest son of Portugal's former captain made his Under-15 debut in 2025 before progressing to the Under-16s, collecting 13 appearances across those two age groups. Portugal next host Bulgaria and Serbia in the first qualifying round for the 2027 Under-17 European Championship, with the top two teams advancing. All their matches will take place at Cidade do Futebol. His name ensures scrutiny, but his father has long balanced ambition for his son with an acknowledgement that a famous pedigree offers no guarantee of success.  "Obviously, I'd love for Cristiano Junior to become a footballer and a top-class player like his father," Ronaldo said in 2016, when his son was six.  REMARKABLE CAREER Two years later, Ronaldo said in an interview with DAZN that he saw some of the traits that have driven his remarkable career in his son's game.  "He's very competitive, he's just like I was when I was little. He doesn't like to lose. He'll turn out just like me - I'm 100 per cent sure of that," he said.  "I enjoy teaching him a few things, but he'll become whatever he wants to be, and I'll always support him."  Portugal won the Under-16 Vlatko Markovic tournament in Croatia in 2025, with Cristianinho mimicking his father's trademark celebration after scoring in a 3-0 semi-final win over Wales.  The teenager spent time in the youth ranks of Juventus and Manchester United before moving to Saudi Arabia in 2023.  Both now play for Al Nassr, albeit at different levels, with Cristianinho scoring three goals in seven youth matches this season.

Source: Reuters

BEIJING/HONG KONG: Hong Kong property developer New World Development on Sunday (Nov 15) proposed a rights issue to raise about HK$24.9 billion (US$3.17 billion), a company filing showed. New World Development has been trying to cut debt, dispose of assets and bolster liquidity amid tight credit conditions and a weak property market. The plan offers shareholders 11 rights shares for every existing share at HK$0.90 each, representing a 26.9 per cent discount to the theoretical ex-rights price of HK$1.23 per share. The subscription price also represents an 81.5 per cent discount to the last closing price.

Controlling shareholder Chow Tai Fook Enterprises (CTFE), which owns about 45.3 per cent of the company, has committed to take up its full entitlement and fully underwrite the remaining shares. The maximum CTFE commitment is about HK$18.7 billion. A CTFE statement said it supports New World Development resuming dividend payments when its financial performance and liquidity permit. The company plans to use about 34 per cent of the proceeds to prepay 10 per cent of about HK$82 billion in bank loans and extend the maturity of the remaining 90 per cent by two years. It plans to use another third to repay debt, including senior notes and deferred distribution of its perpetual securities. After the rights issue, New World's net debt to total equity ratio will drop to 48.3 per cent from 68.3 per cent. The developer aims to reduce total debt by between HK$40 billion and HK$50 billion by the end of 2031 to HK$93 billion to HK$103 billion New World's shares will resume trading on Monday after being suspended on Friday pending the announcement.

Nov 15 : England opener Tom Banton struck a superb century and fast bowler Gus Atkinson claimed four wickets as they beat Australia by 135 runs in the second One-Day International in Adelaide on Sunday to level the three-match series at 1-1. Australia won the toss and elected to bowl, but Banton set the tone for England's imposing total by taking the attack to the hosts from the outset. The right-hander reached the second ODI century of his career from just 86 balls before finishing with 121 off 99 deliveries, including 12 fours and four sixes. After England lost Ben Duckett with the score at 19-1, Banton and Joe Root (62) rebuilt the innings with a 137-run second-wicket partnership, the highest stand for that wicket by an England pair in a 50-over match on Australian soil. Australia briefly worked their way back into the contest with three wickets in the middle overs, but wicketkeeper-batter Jordan Cox counterattacked with 67 off 49 deliveries and all-rounder Will Jacks struck an unbeaten 54 from 40 balls to propel England to 355-6, their highest ODI total on Australian soil.

Matt Renshaw (63) and Cameron Green (64) mounted a spirited fightback to keep Australia in contention, but spinner Liam Dawson removed both batters to extinguish the home side's hopes. Australia's lower order offered some late resistance through Jack Edwards (17), Adam Zampa (18), Spencer Johnson (14) and Riley Meredith (17 not out), but they were eventually bowled out for 220. "We obviously bowled first thinking there might have been a little bit in the wicket, which probably sounds weird to say at the Adelaide Oval, and try to maximise those early overs," Australia captain Mitch Marsh said at the presentation. "I thought they batted really well. We tried a lot through the 50 overs, a few different plans with Meredith bowling bumpers, and all sorts of stuff. "Credit to England. They played well. We know they are a good side. A really rounded side and they showed that tonight." England's attack maintained the pressure throughout, with Atkinson finishing with outstanding figures of 4-28. Dawson and all-rounder Sam Curran chipped in with two wickets apiece as the tourists wrapped up a comprehensive victory. "The whole innings, we looked like we were in control," England captain Harry Brook said. "We countered their bad balls, put them under pressure when we needed to and Banton played an exceptional innings... "The depth that we have means we were able to go on and get that 350." Australia had won the opening ODI in Perth by seven wickets, with the series now set for a decider in Hobart on Wednesday.

MANILA: The Singapore-Indonesia joint task force probing firms linked to haze-causing fires should expand to cover all Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) members, Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Sunday (Nov 15). Speaking at the retreat session of the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila, Mr Wong said the task force – first announced in October – aims to improve coordination and information-sharing as both sides pursue those responsible for the fires. The task force "doesn’t have to be a bilateral platform", he said. "It should be an ASEAN-wide platform where we can share information more readily and where we can share evidence on those that are responsible, because fires can happen in any country in ASEAN, and we want to send a very clear message to all companies that this is not the way to go about clearing forests," he added.

"If anyone is caught doing this, across ASEAN, we will share information, we will take action, and we will hold companies responsible. I think that is something we should strive to do as part of ASEAN." The bloc already has mechanisms to achieve this, such as the Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution, which he hoped could be strengthened. Beyond extinguishing the fires, ASEAN must also work to prevent a recurrence, he said. Mr Wong also commended Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto for his efforts in investigating the cause of the fires and holding errant companies accountable. Singapore is doing the same with Singapore-based firms that may be responsible or linked to companies not upholding good practices in clearing forests, he added. Earlier this month, Singapore amended its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act to strengthen action against such firms. He thanked Mr Prabowo for "taking unprecedented efforts" to tackle the fires, which were worsened this year by climate change and a "very unusual El Nino season that resulted in a very dry spell". "I also want to express my appreciation for the many, many Indonesian emergency personnel and firefighters, who work tirelessly in very dangerous conditions," added Mr Wong. "We extend our deepest appreciation to them, and we send our best wishes for the recovery of those who are injured."

Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim also raised the haze issue earlier in the summit’s plenary session. He said Malaysia has proposed Science Diplomacy and Sustainable Haze Fund initiatives through the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee framework, Malaysian news outlet the Star reported. Mr Anwar said the proposals aim to improve scientific collaboration, promote evidence-based decision-making and secure sustainable funding for the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution. Malaysia will push these priorities at the Conference of the Parties to the agreement next month and through its chairmanship of the steering committee next year, he added. REGIONAL TENSIONS Mr Wong also called on ASEAN members to work together to address border tensions between Thailand and Cambodia. "Singapore understands that this is a deeply emotive issue for the peoples of both countries. We would encourage both sides to continue exercising restraint, avoid escalation, and resolve differences through dialogue, including through established bilateral mechanisms," he said. Singapore will continue to support the process, especially as it takes on the chairmanship of the ASEAN Observer Team next year, he added. On Myanmar, Mr Wong said the bloc's member states have "a strong desire" to see the country "return to the ASEAN family in terms of its political participation" at some point. Engagement must be two-way, he said, with Myanmar showing "concrete actions that demonstrate real progress" in line with the Five-Point Consensus. This includes progress on humanitarian assistance, dialogue with stakeholders and the cessation of violence.

ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus

Following a 2021 military coup, ASEAN has excluded Myanmar from high-level meetings as it has yet to make meaningful progress on the bloc's Five-Point Consensus to end hostilities. During a meeting in April 2021, all ASEAN leaders reached a consensus about the situation in Myanmar. The five points are: First, there shall be immediate cessation of violence in Myanmar and all parties shall exercise utmost restraint. Second, constructive dialogue among all parties concerned shall commence to seek a peaceful solution in the interests of the people. Third, a special envoy of the ASEAN chair shall facilitate mediation of the dialogue process, with the assistance of the secretary-general of ASEAN. Fourth, ASEAN shall provide humanitarian assistance through the AHA Centre. Fifth, the special envoy and delegation shall visit Myanmar to meet with all parties concerned. Source: Reuters

He acknowledged the Myanmar representative’s previous claim that not all violence is within the Myanmar government’s control, as some is committed by ethnic armed organisations. "We recognise that, but at the same time we also want to make sure that there should not be any violence committed by the Myanmar government, and there should be effort in terms of a sustained reduction of violence in Myanmar, as far as the government is concerned," Mr Wong said. Such steps would help restore stability in the country and build a long-term solution that is owned and led by Myanmar itself, ultimately benefiting its people, he said. "We would like to see that outcome eventually, but it takes two hands to clap," he said. "ASEAN can do more to engage, and Myanmar should also show its readiness to work constructively with ASEAN towards this goal. If we are united on both sides, hopefully we can see good progress on this."

Nov 15 : India pulled off a remarkable escape in Tauranga on Sunday, with Arshdeep Singh leading a pace-led fightback to secure a thrilling 22-run win over New Zealand and seal the five-match one-day international series 3-1. Defending a modest 209, India looked destined for defeat as New Zealand cruised to 64-1 before the visitors' pacers sparked a dramatic collapse, with the hosts losing five wickets for 55 runs before crashing out on 187 in 48.1 overs. Put in to bat, India made a cautious start, mindful of their crushing 244-run defeat in the previous ODI, but their approach unravelled as New Zealand's bowlers ripped through the top order before Axar Patel and Ishan Kishan helped the visitors recover to 209 all out in 42.1 overs. New Zealand openers Will Young and Nick Kelly capitalised on the platform laid by their bowlers and looked on course for a comfortable chase before India's bowlers breathed life into the contest in the middle overs, relentlessly attacking the stumps and denying the hosts any opportunity to counterattack.

Yash Thakur built pressure with a disciplined spell, while Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep struck at regular intervals as the hosts slumped from 64-1 to 119-6. Dean Foxcroft top-scored with 31 off 42 balls and attempted to steady the innings as wickets tumbled around him, but Yash removed him to claim his maiden ODI wicket. Captain Mitchell Santner's 24 off 31 balls offered resistance, but India's bowlers continued to chip away and eventually wrapped up the tail to complete a memorable victory. "We didn't have a great batting but our bowlers all bowled with the same direction and we were able to execute," said captain Shreyas Iyer, who backed his seamers for the bulk of the innings before turning to spin in the 36th over. "This whole series was not a good one for batters but the mindset is to take the team through irrespective of the conditions." Player of the Match Arshdeep finished with figures of 3-30, while Siraj and spinner Patel picked up two wickets apiece and the remaining bowlers claimed one each. "India bowled really well tonight," Santner said. "Shreyas did a great job rotating his seamers and holding Axar back. If we took each partnership a little longer, we would've won the game. It was a great bowling performance from India." Earlier, New Zealand's attack kept India on the back foot throughout, with fast bowler Matthew Fisher striking early to remove veterans Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli. Patel, who survived two chances, stitched together a 52-run partnership with Shreyas (22) before combining with Kishan in a bid to rebuild the innings. Patel and Kishan scored 46 apiece, while Naman Dhir contributed a late 22 before Jacob Duffy and Santner wrapped up the tail. Santner (3-47) and Duffy (3-60) claimed three wickets each, while Fisher finished with two. India and New Zealand will next meet in a two-test series beginning on November 19.

Nov 15 : Former Australia test bowler Chadd Sayers backed Usman Khawaja's claims about the Sandpapergate scandal on Sunday, saying he believes everyone in the side during the 2018 tour of South Africa knew sandpaper was being used to alter the condition of the ball. The tampering, discovered during the third test at Newlands in Cape Town, led to former captain Steve Smith and vice captain David Warner being banned for 12 months by Cricket Australia (CA) from elite cricket. Cameron Bancroft received a nine-month suspension for his part in the incident. Khawaja wrote in his autobiography "Sabr: Finding my way in Cricket and Life", released on Tuesday, that knowledge of the plan was not limited to the three players who were punished and was more widespread within the team. In the wake of the new allegations, CA has ruled out reopening its 2018 investigation, while Warner has accused the sports body of orchestrating a cover-up by ignoring key witnesses and seeking to pin blame on three players.

"I believe that everyone in that side knew what was going on and what was being used," Sayers told SEN radio. Sayers, 39, also echoed Khawaja's claim that sandpaper was used during the second test at Port Elizabeth, saying he was the player who removed it from the field. "It (sandpaper) was given to me to take off, so that wasn't planned or anything. I was just the player who took the drinks out at the time ... it was passed on to me," he said. Sayers, who made his only test appearance for Australia in the fourth test of the 2018 South Africa tour, said he was never interviewed as part of CA's inquiry. He added that maybe it was because he was 12th man and didn't play in the game or perhaps because he knew too much information. "I'm not too sure," he said. MANILA: Southeast Asian leaders said on Sunday (Nov 15) they may consider gradually restoring Myanmar's full political representation in the regional bloc, if the country makes progress on their longstanding plan to resolve its five-year-old crisis. Leaders of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations agreed at a summit in Manila to maintain their policy of excluding Myanmar from full political representation at ASEAN summits and foreign ministers' meetings for now. But they said they had agreed to pursue a "calibrated engagement" through a "phased and progress-based" approach, if Myanmar makes "sustained and concrete" progress on the bloc's proposed plan, known as the five-point consensus, or 5PC.

ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus

Following a 2021 military coup , ASEAN has excluded Myanmar from high-level meetings as it has yet to make meaningful progress on the bloc's Five-Point Consensus to end hostilities.  During a meeting in April 2021, all ASEAN leaders reached a consensus about the situation in Myanmar. The five points are: First, there shall be immediate cessation of violence in Myanmar and all parties shall exercise utmost restraint. Second, constructive dialogue among all parties concerned shall commence to seek a peaceful solution in the interests of the people. Third, a special envoy of the ASEAN chair shall facilitate mediation of the dialogue process, with the assistance of the secretary-general of ASEAN. Fourth, ASEAN shall provide humanitarian assistance through the AHA Centre. Fifth, the special envoy and delegation shall visit Myanmar to meet with all parties concerned.

And in a notable step, the bloc also appeared to endorse bilateral outreach to Myanmar among its member countries.

Thailand and several other ASEAN members have stepped up engagement with Myanmar in recent months, creating new pressure on the bloc to ease its ban on Myanmar's military-backed leaders attending its high-level meetings. "Subject to sustained and concrete progress in the implementation of the 5PC by Myanmar, ASEAN may consider the gradual restoration of Myanmar's full political representation," the leaders said in a joint decision adopted at the summit. "We also encourage efforts by individual ASEAN Member States through constructive engagement with all relevant stakeholders, in consultation with the ASEAN Chair, to advance substantive progress in the implementation of the 5PC," they said. ASEAN's five-point consensus, adopted soon after the military seized power in Myanmar in 2021, calls for an immediate end to violence there and for the launch of constructive dialogue among all parties. It offers ASEAN mediation and humanitarian assistance. Myanmar's army-backed government wants to normalise ties with ASEAN. The country has been in turmoil since the military ousted Nobel Peace Prize winner Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government, triggering a civil war that the UN estimates has killed 100,000 people and displaced more than 3.5 million. Coup leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing's military has received support from China, India and Russia. His administration has gained increasing international recognition in recent months, including secret talks with US officials as President Donald Trump's administration reverses years of isolation.
